And lately, these little billing errors keep showing up at my work... just tiny discrepancies that someone who isn't paying attention might just brush off as a mistake, but I see them. I know what they mean. 

And it's not just the finances, it's our reputation, too. I'll go to church on Sunday, and suddenly someone I've sat next to for years is acting funny toward me, giving me these strange looks, or cutting a conversation short for no reason at all. And people tell me I'm overthinking it, they pull up the bank records or the office logs and say, look, everything is fine, it's just a typo, but they don't see the whole picture. No matter what records anyone pulls up, no matter what paperwork they try to show me, I know for a fact it all ties back to his family pulling strings behind the scenes to ruin us. They're just very, very careful about hiding it, but I know exactly what they're doing.

That is exactly the problem, doctor, and it is exactly why I'm sitting here today. Because, like I was just saying, I have been trying for months to get people to understand what his family is doing, and it feels like I am entirely alone in this. I am the only one who seems to actually open my eyes and notice, or at least, I'm the only one willing to connect the dots.

And my husband, he's completely blind to it. I'll tell him about how someone at church suddenly acts funny toward me, like how Mary practically sprinted the other way after service last week instead of asking about the bake sale like she usually does, and he just makes excuses for them. He says she was probably just rushing to get home to check on her roast. 

It drives me absolutely crazy, it really does, because I am trying to protect us. And no matter what records anyone pulls up, no matter what bank statements or office logs they try to put in front of my face to say everything is perfectly normal, I know it ties back to his family. I know it does. They are quietly messing with our money and our good name, and they are doing it so meticulously, so underhandedly, that everyone else just thinks I'm overreacting or seeing things that aren't there. But I'm not. I see the whole pattern. It's just incredibly isolating to be the only one who realizes we're being sabotaged while everyone else just goes about their day.
Have you ever considered the possibility that your husband's family might not be involved in the things you're noticing?

Considered it? Well, I mean... I'm a rational person, doctor, I really am. So of course, at the very beginning of all this, I sat myself down—I remember I was sitting at the kitchen table with a cup of coffee—and I thought to myself, 'Maybe I'm just tired. Maybe it's just a string of coincidences.' I really tried to give them the benefit of the doubt, I did. I tried to tell myself that those little billing errors showing up at work were just because we had a recent system update, or maybe the other clerks were just rushing their data entry and making silly mistakes. And I tried to tell myself that when people at church suddenly act funny toward me, you know, like they're hiding something or cutting me off, that maybe they're just distracted with their own lives. 

But you can only make excuses for so long before you have to look at the reality of the situation! Because for months now, I’ve been trying to get people to understand that my husband’s family is quietly messing with our money and our good name. It's not a coincidence when it keeps happening over and over and over again, in these very specific ways.

But they don't get how deep this goes or how careful his family is being. No matter what records anyone pulls up, no matter what paperwork they try to shove in my face, I know it ties back to them. I know it does. Because who else would do this? His mother never liked me, not since the day we got married twenty years ago, and his sister is always asking these little probing questions about our finances. So, yes, I tried to consider that maybe they weren't involved, but the proof is just too overwhelming. They are pulling the strings, doctor, and it just absolutely exhausts me that I have to sit here and justify what is so plainly obvious to anyone who would just take five minutes to really look at the ledger.

Doubted it? I mean... doctor, I feel like we might be going in circles just a little bit here, because like I was just trying to explain a minute ago, I really don't have the luxury of doubting it anymore. I just don't. I mean, for months now—months and months—I’ve been trying to get people to understand that my husband’s family is quietly, very methodically, messing with our money and our good name. How can I doubt it when the evidence is literally popping up over and over again? 

I go into the office, I sit down at my desk, I boot up the software—software I have used for years, mind you, I know it inside and out, I know every shortcut—and there they are. Those little billing errors. Just waiting for me. And it's not just the financial side of things, it's the social side, too.
